caption_en:
How to build a country. Hard mode. This time: resurrect a dead language. 📘

1. Your people arrive from 70+ countries (3.09M immigrants 1948 to 2011, Jewish Virtual Library).
2. Pick a language with no native speakers for about 1,700 years (spoken Hebrew died out around 200 CE: Kutscher, Academy of the Hebrew Language).
3. Eliezer Ben-Yehuda raises his son Itamar Ben-Avi (born 1882) in Hebrew, one of its first native speakers in modern times.
4. Invent words: millon (dictionary), glida (ice cream), bubba (doll), havita (omelette). His dictionary: 17 volumes, 1908 to 1959 (Academy of the Hebrew Language).
5. 1913: the Technikum in Haifa plans science classes in German. Teachers and students walk out. Feb 1914: Hebrew wins (Encyclopaedia Judaica).
6. Ulpan Hebrew classes for newcomers, since 1949 (Jewish Agency).
7. Today: over 9 million speakers (Israel CBS 2023 survey; National Geographic 2023). The most successful language revival in history (Grenoble and Whaley, 2005).

He didn't do it alone: teachers, parents and kids did. And if a country can learn a dead language, you can learn a living one.

Photos (Wikimedia Commons): PikiWiki Israel; Craig Talbert CC BY 2.0; Shlomo Narinsky; GPO Israel; Ya'ackov Ben-Dov; Matson Collection, LOC; Leni Sonnenfeld; Korenn CC BY-SA 4.0. AI voice.

Send this to someone learning a language.
caption_he:
איך בונים מדינה, רמת קושי: קשה. הפעם: מחיים שפה מתה.
עולים מיותר מ־70 מדינות. שפה בלי דוברי אם כ־1,700 שנה. אליעזר בן־יהודה מגדל את איתמר (1882) בעברית. מילון, גלידה, בובה, חביתה. מלחמת השפות ב־1913 בטכניון. אולפן מאז 1949. היום: יותר מ־9 מיליון דוברים.
אם מדינה שלמה למדה שפה מתה, גם אתם יכולים ללמוד שפה חיה.

lines.line: How to build a country. Hard mode. Resurrect a dead language.
Step one: your people arrive from more than seventy countries.
Yiddish. Arabic. Ladino. Russian. Persian. Amharic. Good luck with the first meeting.
Step two: pick a language nobody has spoken as a mother tongue for about seventeen hundred years.
Step three: one man, Eliezer Ben-Yehuda, raises his son in it.
Itamar, born eighteen eighty two. One of the first native speakers in modern times.
Step four: no word for ice cream? Invent one.
Then the dictionary. Seventeen volumes. Fifty one years.
Step five: nineteen thirteen. Your technical college plans to teach science in German.
Teachers and students walk out. February nineteen fourteen: Hebrew wins.
Step six: Hebrew class for every wave of newcomers. The ulpan, since nineteen forty nine.
Step seven: today, over nine million people speak it.
Linguists call it the most successful language revival in history.
If a country can learn a dead language, you can learn a living one.
Now. How do you build a country?
